```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE)
library(gsDesignNB)
library(ggplot2)
library(lt)
```

## Reference design

`gsNBPower()` evaluates an existing design without resizing enrollment to recover
target power. All time quantities below are in months. Information is evaluated
at the planned calendar dates unless an explicit timing requirement is supplied.

```{r reference}
fixed <- sample_size_nbinom(
  lambda1 = 1.5 / 12, lambda2 = 1 / 12, dispersion = 0.5,
  power = 0.9, accrual_rate = 1, accrual_duration = 12,
  trial_duration = 24, dropout_rate = -log(0.95) / 12,
  max_followup = 12, event_gap = 20 / 30.4375
)
design <- gsDesignNB::toInteger(gsNB(fixed, test.type = 1))
reference <- gsNBPower(design)
reference$look_results |>
  lt::lt()
```

Expected information agrees with the rounded planning design. Sample size and
analysis dates remain unchanged when evaluating a different treatment rate.
The reported expected resources account for stopping at any active boundary,
with every remaining trial ending at the final decision.

## Scenario sensitivity

The following curves keep one design fixed. They are not separate designs each
resized to have 90% power. Dispersion, event rates, follow-up, dropout, and
piecewise accrual can all be changed in the same way.

```{r curves}
grid <- expand.grid(
  rate_ratio = seq(0.4, 1.1, by = 0.05), dispersion = c(0.5, 1),
  spending = c("min_planned_actual", "planned_final", "expected_final", "calendar"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
grid$power <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(index) {
  gsNBPower(
    design, lambda2 = fixed$inputs$lambda1 * grid$rate_ratio[index],
    dispersion = grid$dispersion[index], spending = grid$spending[index]
  )$power
}, numeric(1))
ggplot(grid, aes(rate_ratio, power, color = spending)) +
  geom_line() + facet_wrap(~ dispersion, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(x = "True experimental/control rate ratio", y = "Asymptotic power",
       color = "Spending strategy") + theme_minimal()
```

Recomputed boundaries spend the full upper error budget at the final analysis.
`min_planned_actual` caps interim spending at both planned and accumulated
information. `planned_final` uses the original final information denominator.
`expected_final` uses scenario-expected final information; during a trial this
denominator must be projected from currently available data. `calendar` uses
calendar fractions. Explicit spending times inherited from the design take
precedence over these rules.

```{r score-wald}
comparisons <- expand.grid(
  test_type = c("score", "wald"), boundary_update = c("fixed", "recompute"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
comparisons$power <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(comparisons)), function(index) {
  gsNBPower(design, lambda2 = 0.1, test_type = comparisons$test_type[index],
            boundary_update = comparisons$boundary_update[index])$power
}, numeric(1))
lt::lt(comparisons)
```

The score approximation uses separate null and alternative variances. Both
approximations assume a canonical cross-look covariance structure; finite-sample
score calibration and information-estimation uncertainty require simulation.
Fixed numerical bounds need not retain nominal Type I error under different
information fractions.

## Combined timing requirements

Targets combine with AND. The final analysis stays at its hard calendar deadline.
An unreachable interim is reported as skipped, rather than creating another test
at the same final information.

```{r timing}
information_timing <- gsNBPower(
  design, planned_calendar = c(NA, NA, 24),
  target_info = c(design$n.I[1:2], NA)
)
minimum_age <- gsNBPower(
  design, min_n = c(design$n_total[3], NA, NA),
  min_followup = c(3, NA, NA)
)
shortfall <- gsNBPower(design, lambda1 = 0.02, lambda2 = 0.014,
                       target_info = c(design$n.I[1:2], NA))
lt::lt(shortfall$look_results)
```

`min_n` and `min_followup` refer to randomized subjects' calendar age, not to
patients who remain observed without dropout. Expected target-hitting dates are
deterministic planning approximations, not means of random simulated dates.

## Reusing completed simulations

The shipped GS cache contains 3,600 Wald trials and their numerical planning
bounds. Reclassifying the saved Z paths against those fixed bounds provides a
matched comparison without generating additional trials. Its original summary
used observed-information-updated boundaries and answers a different question.

```{r cached-comparison}
cache_path <- system.file("extdata", "gs_simulation_results.rds", package = "gsDesignNB")
if (!nzchar(cache_path)) cache_path <- "../inst/extdata/gs_simulation_results.rds"
cache <- readRDS(cache_path)
checked <- check_gs_bound(cache$sim_res, cache$gs_nb,
                          info_col = "info_unblinded_ml", boundary_update = "fixed")
rejected <- aggregate(cross_upper ~ sim, checked, any)$cross_upper
interval <- binom.test(sum(rejected), length(rejected))$conf.int
comparison <- data.frame(
  asymptotic = gsNBPower(cache$gs_nb, boundary_update = "fixed")$power,
  simulated = mean(rejected), lower = interval[1], upper = interval[2],
  replicates = length(rejected)
)
lt::lt(comparison)
```

This comparator includes the cache's futility rule. The study article separately
evaluates information estimators and spending strategies under null and
alternative scenarios.

## Blinded final-information projection

The existing blinded SSR calculation also returns `info_projected` at the
supplied enrollment and final date, without increasing sample size. Its
`target_info` is a fixed-design power target and must not be substituted for
projected GS final information.

```{r blinded-workflow, eval=FALSE}
blinded <- blinded_ssr(
  interim_data, lambda1_planning = 1.5 / 12, lambda2_planning = 1 / 12,
  accrual_rate = design$n_total[3] / 12, accrual_duration = 12,
  trial_duration = 24, max_followup = 12, event_gap = 20 / 30.4375,
  analysis_time = interim_date
)
interim_fraction <- blinded$blinded_info / blinded$info_projected
```

Projection uncertainty, pooled-rate splitting, and failed nuisance fits are
measured in the simulation study. No asymptotic result alone establishes Type I
error control for estimated, data-dependent spending.
